Text no longer runs off the foot of a page, and a table over an empty list comes out whole.

**Upgrade from any earlier version if your tables can hold long cells, or lists that can be empty.** Both
faults lost or garbled text without an error. Documents without those shapes come out as they did, to the
byte. Nothing was removed or renamed in the public API, and the template format has no new properties.

## Fixed: text ran off the foot of the page

A document drew past the foot of a page, and the part below it never reached the paper. Nothing failed.

- **A table row taller than a page**, first on its page, was laid whole. Text went on down to 968 mm on a
  page of 297, in one page, where the same row with anything above it took four pages and lost nothing. A
  row that only overflowed under its own header did the same. Both are cut between two lines now and carry
  on overleaf, under the header if it repeats.
- **A row whose long text is rich** (`AdvancedTextItem`) was never cut, wherever it stood. Everything the
  content editor writes is rich text, so this was every long cell it produced. It is cut like plain text now,
  each line keeping its own height.
- **The first item of a stacked group near the foot of a page** went off the page instead of moving to the
  next one: a picture, a grid, a row kept whole. The group moves now, with any heading set to `KeepWithNext`
  above it.
- **What was left of a row no page could hold** was started again from its first line, so its words came out
  twice. It carries on from where it had got to.

## New: what cannot be cut says so

Some things still cannot go overleaf: a picture taller than the page, a group in a table cell, a stated
height, something marked `KeepTogether`. They go down as they are, and the part below the foot is not on the
paper. That now raises `fits.overflow`, a warning in `LayoutResult.Issues`, one for each thing to put right.
`ReportRenderer.Render` returns that result, so reading it takes one line:

```csharp
LayoutResult layout = ReportRenderer.Render(report, backend);
foreach (TemplateIssue issue in layout.Issues)
    log.Warn($"{issue.Rule}, {issue.Where}: {issue.Message}");
```

`frisket render` now prints these on standard error, along with the two it never showed: `fits.pageLimit` and
`fits.importedPage`.

## Fixed: a table over an empty list

With a list that turned out empty and an `EmptyText` to show:

- the table's header and the message printed their tokens as typed, braces and all; both are filled now,
  reading the data outside the list;
- the message sat in the first column at the document's default size, breaking mid-word in a narrow one. It
  takes every column now, centred, in the font of the first text the lines hold;
- the row had one cell in a table of several, so **PDF/UA refused the file**. It declares its span now, in the
  PDF and in the mail output.

`TemplateFields.Check` now reads `EmptyText` too, and flags a misspelt name or a field of an entry, since there
is no entry to read when the message shows.

An image grid keeps its message in its first cell. Its token is filled, and nothing else changes there.

## Worth checking

- **Long tables and groups near the foot of a page** may paginate differently, since what used to overrun the
  page now moves or carries on. That is the fix, and page numbers after it can change.
- **`MissingField.Fail`** can now refuse a document over a token in the header or `EmptyText` of an empty list.
  Those tokens were never read before. With the default, a token the data does not answer stays on the page as
  typed, as it does anywhere else.
- **A filled document saved as JSON and read back** loses the empty-list row's span, which only the binder can
  set, and `sound.raggedTable` then says so. Render from the template and the data rather than from a saved
  filled copy.
